schema_grounding_notes: protein_id: UniProt canonical accession (e.g. 'P04637'). Always emit protein_name alongside protein_id in output — never return a protein_id without the human-readable protein name.
gene_symbol: HGNC official symbol only — p53→TP53.
hgnc: stored WITH the 'HGNC:' prefix (e.g. 'HGNC:11998'). When a user provides a bare integer HGNC ID, prepend 'HGNC:' before filtering.
ensembl_accession: normalised to the bare ENSG form (e.g. 'ENSG00000141510'); the loader strips the version and isoform suffix. Match external Ensembl IDs on this bare form.

aspect: single-character code — 'F' = Molecular Function, 'P' = Biological Process, 'C' = Cellular Component. When the user says 'molecular function', filter aspect = 'F'; 'biological process' → 'P'; 'cellular component' or 'location' → 'C'.

qualifier: when the user asks what a protein 'does' or its 'function', filter qualifier = 'enables' (aspect F); for 'where is the protein located', DO NOT filter by qualifier — use aspect=['C'] only and include all qualifier values (located_in, is_active_in, part_of, colocalizes_with are all location-relevant; filtering to located_in/part_of alone drops ~15% of cellular component annotations).

evidence: IEA = computationally inferred; TAS = traceable author statement; IDA/IPI/IBA/ISS/HDA/IC/HMP = experimental or curator evidence. When the user asks for 'experimental evidence', include IDA, IPI, HDA, IMP, IEP; exclude IEA.
variant_type: 'LP/P' means the variant is clinically significant (pathogenic); 'LB/B' means benign; 'US' means uncertain. When the user asks for 'pathogenic variants', filter variant_type = 'LP/P'.
swiss_prot_change: HGVS protein notation (e.g. 'p.Arg175His'). Accepts standard HGVS p. format from users.
dbsnp: stored with 'rs' prefix (e.g. 'rs28934578'). Users may omit the 'rs' prefix — prepend it before filtering.
disease_name: free-text string often including MIM number in brackets. Use LIKE/contains matching rather than exact match for disease lookups.

omim_id: bare OMIM disease integer (e.g. '151623'), no 'OMIM:'/'MIM:' prefix; extracted from disease_name's '[MIM:NNNNNN]' tag. Null for ~54% of variant_disease rows. disease_id is always null — use omim_id or disease_name instead.
protein_master_table_uniprot: all 20,431 rows are Swiss-Prot reviewed human proteins (organism = 'Homo sapiens (Human)', reviewed = 'true'). No need to filter by reviewed status.

gene_symbol lookups: use protein_master_table_uniprot.gene_symbol as the canonical filter (it is the sole queryable gene_symbol column). For multi-gene proteins or secondary gene mappings, reach gene_protein_association_uniprot via protein_id FK from protein_master_table. (runtime table name: gene_protein_association_uniprot)

id_mapping_uniprot: use when the user provides an Ensembl, RefSeq, GeneID, HGNC, or other external ID and needs the UniProt accession. Filter by db column to select the database type (valid values: Ensembl, Ensembl_PRO, Ensembl_TRS, GeneID, Gene_Name, Gene_Synonym, HGNC, RefSeq, RefSeq_NT, UniProtKB-ID).
keyword_master_uniprot: 1,201 rows defining UniProt's controlled keyword vocabulary. Query this table to look up keyword definitions, synonyms, or hierarchies.
subcell_location_uniprot: 566 rows defining UniProt's subcellular location vocabulary. Query this for location definitions, GO cross-references, or location hierarchies.
variant_disease_uniprot: 84,476 natural variant records from Swiss-Prot; disease_id is always null — use omim_id (bare OMIM integer, ~46% populated) or disease_name for disease-based filtering.

co_output_rules.reason: UniProt accessions (e.g. P04637) are opaque; protein_name must always accompany protein_id in output
Always show gene_symbol alongside protein_id so users can relate protein to gene
GO IDs are opaque; aspect (F/P/C) and qualifier provide essential context for any GO annotation
VAR_ feature IDs are internal; always show the protein change notation alongside
SL- subcellular IDs are opaque; always show subcell_name
KW- keyword IDs are opaque; always show keyword_name

few_shot_examples.question: What are the molecular functions of EGFR?
few_shot_examples.note: gene→GO molecular function query — gene_symbol is the FILTER. aspect=['F'] and qualifier=['enables'] are BOTH required filters for molecular function. EGFR (P00533) has GO:0004672 (protein kinase activity, IEA), GO:0004709 (MAP kinase kinase kinase activity, evidence=NAS). go_id is the output.

few_shot_examples.question: Where is TP53 located in the cell?
few_shot_examples.note: gene→cellular component GO query — gene_symbol is the FILTER. aspect=['C'] is a required filter. Returns GO cellular component terms for TP53, e.g. GO:0005634 (nucleus), GO:0016604 (nuclear body, PML), GO:0005829 (cytosol). Do NOT filter qualifier — include all aspect=C rows (located_in, is_active_in, part_of, colocalizes_with). TP53 has 37 GO aspect=C annotations. Note: for curated SL-location names (e.g. 'Nucleus', 'Cytoplasm') use protein_subcell_uniprot instead.

few_shot_examples.question: Which pathogenic variants of BRCA1 are in UniProt?
few_shot_examples.note: gene→variant query with pathogenicity filter — gene_symbol + variant_type=['LP/P'] are BOTH filters. BRCA1 (P38398) LP/P variants include p.Leu22Ser (rs80357438, Breast cancer), p.Cys61Gly (rs28897672). swiss_prot_change and disease_name are outputs. variant_type='LP/P' means Likely Pathogenic/Pathogenic.

few_shot_examples.question: What GO annotations does TP53 have with IDA experimental evidence?
few_shot_examples.note: evidence-filtered GO query — gene_symbol + evidence=['IDA'] are BOTH filters. IDA = Inferred from Direct Assay (experimental). TP53 (P04637) has multiple IDA-evidenced GO annotations. aspect should be 'requested' (not a filter) since no specific aspect was specified.

few_shot_examples.question: What UniProt keywords are annotated for EGFR?
few_shot_examples.note: gene→keyword query — gene_symbol is the FILTER. keyword_name is the output. EGFR (P00533) keywords include Kinase, Transferase, Secreted, Golgi apparatus, Disease variant. Uses protein_keyword_uniprot joined to keyword_master_uniprot on keyword_id.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What are the GO terms for TP53?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: GO annotation query: gene_symbol (WHERE filter on TP53), go_id (SELECT output), aspect and qualifier (GO context co-outputs). disease_name, variant_type, subcell_name, and keyword_name are IRRELEVANT — this is a GO term question, not a disease, variant, or keyword question.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What diseases are associated with BRCA1?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: Disease association query: gene_symbol (WHERE filter on BRCA1), disease_name (SELECT output). GO columns (go_id, aspect, qualifier), keyword_name, and subcell_name are IRRELEVANT. Note: variant-level disease associations live in variant_disease_uniprot — if the question asks only for disease names without variant details, disease_name alone is sufficient.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What domains does EGFR have?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: Protein domain/keyword query: gene_symbol (WHERE filter on EGFR), keyword_name (SELECT output — UniProt encodes domain membership via functional keywords such as 'Kinase', 'Receptor', 'Transmembrane', 'EGF-like domain'). GO columns, disease_name, and subcell_name are IRRELEVANT to a domain question.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Where in the cell is TP53 located?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: Subcellular localisation query: gene_symbol (WHERE filter on TP53), subcell_name (SELECT output from subcell_location_uniprot via protein_subcell_uniprot). GO columns (go_id, aspect, qualifier), disease_name, keyword_name, and variant columns are IRRELEVANT — the question is about cellular location only.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What variants in BRCA1 cause disease?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: Variant-disease query: gene_symbol (WHERE filter on BRCA1), swiss_prot_change + variant_type (SELECT outputs — the variant details), disease_name (SELECT output — associated disease). GO columns (go_id, aspect, qualifier), keyword_name, and subcell_name are IRRELEVANT to a variant-disease question.

orchestrator_examples.question: What are the molecular functions of EGFR?
orchestrator_examples.reasoning: For molecular function queries, aspect=['F'] alone is insufficient — qualifier=['enables'] must also be a filter because GO aspect F includes 'contributes_to' and other non-enabling relations. mapper_2 omitted qualifier, which would include non-function relations. EGFR has both 'enables' (e.g. GO:0004672) and 'contributes_to' (e.g. GO:0005006) in aspect F.

orchestrator_examples.question: Which pathogenic variants of BRCA1 are in UniProt?
orchestrator_examples.reasoning: The user asked for 'pathogenic' variants → variant_type=['LP/P'] is a mandatory filter. mapper_2 dropped the pathogenicity filter, returning all 3 variant_type categories (LP/P, LB/B, US) mixed together. variant_type enum — LP/P = pathogenic, LB/B = benign, US = uncertain significance.

orchestrator_examples.question: What GO annotations does TP53 have?
orchestrator_examples.reasoning: The question asks for GO annotations with no qualifier or evidence filter specified — do not add qualifier or evidence unless explicitly requested. mapper_2 hallucinated unrequested qualifier and evidence columns. aspect='requested' is correct since the question asks for all GO annotations regardless of aspect (F/P/C).

orchestrator_examples.question: What is the UniProt entry for TP53?
orchestrator_examples.reasoning: A protein lookup question should return protein_id (P04637), protein_name ('Cellular tumor antigen p53'), and entry_name ('P53_HUMAN'). mapper_2 omitted protein_name and entry_name. co_output_rules automatically adds protein_name and gene_symbol when protein_id is requested, but entry_name must be explicit.

_comment: Schema rules for uniprot. Injected into expander/filter/mapper prompts at runtime. GENERATED from dbs/uniprot/schema.yaml by scripts/gen_schema.py — DO NOT EDIT.
db_description: UniProt — Swiss-Prot manually reviewed protein knowledgebase for Homo sapiens (20,431 proteins); covers protein identity, Gene Ontology annotations, subcellular locations, functional keywords, natural variant–disease associations, and cross-database ID mappings. Also provides: free-text CC FUNCTION annotations via protein_function_uniprot (17K proteins), post-translational modification sites with position/modification/enzymes via ptm_sites_uniprot (56K sites), and protein–protein interaction data (BINARY partners + SUBUNIT complex text) via protein_interaction_uniprot (192K rows).

column_notes_override.protein_id: UniProt canonical accession (e.g. 'P04637'). Always output alongside protein_name and gene_symbol, never alone.
column_notes_override.hgnc: Stored WITH 'HGNC:' prefix (e.g. 'HGNC:11998'). Prepend prefix to bare integer user input.
column_notes_override.evidence: GO evidence code: IEA = electronic inference; TAS = author statement; IDA/IPI/IBA = experimental.
column_notes_override.aspect: GO namespace: 'F' = Molecular Function, 'P' = Biological Process, 'C' = Cellular Component.
column_notes_override.variant_type: Clinical significance: 'LP/P' = pathogenic, 'LB/B' = benign, 'US' = uncertain significance.
